title: The Artin–Schreier sequence
statement:
Let $C$ be a curve [def-sc-curves] over the algebraically closed field $k$, of characteristic $p>0$, and let $C_{\Et}$ be its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $\mathbf G_a=(\mathcal O_C)_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the etale sheaf $U\mapsto\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ associated with the structure sheaf [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module] (a sheaf by [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-descent]), an object of the abelian category $\Ab(C_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and let $\mathbf F_p$ be the constant sheaf with value $\mathbf Z/p\mathbf Z$ [def-sc-constant-sheaves]. Let $\wp:\mathbf G_a\to\mathbf G_a$ be the morphism $\wp_U(x)=x^p-x$, and let $\iota:\mathbf F_p\to\mathbf G_a$ be the morphism induced, by the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], by the morphism of presheaves $c\mapsto c\cdot1\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ from the constant presheaf $U\mapsto\mathbf Z/p\mathbf Z$. Then the sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow\mathbf F_p\xrightarrow{\ \iota\ }\mathbf G_a
\xrightarrow{\ \wp\ }\mathbf G_a\longrightarrow0,
\qquad \wp(x)=x^p-x,
$$

is a short exact sequence of $\Ab(C_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]: $\iota$ is a monomorphism, $\wp$ is an epimorphism, and $\iota$ is a kernel of $\wp$.

proof.text: *The maps.* Every object $u:U\to C$ of $C_{\Et}$ is a $k$-scheme, so $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)=\Gamma(U,u^*\mathcal O_C)=\mathbf G_a(U)$ [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module] is a $k$-algebra and $p\cdot1=0$ in it. Hence $\wp_U(x)=x^p-x$ is additive ($(x+y)^p=x^p+y^p$ in characteristic $p$) and commutes with the restriction maps, which are ring homomorphisms: $\wp$ is a morphism of $\Ab(C_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Likewise $c\mapsto c\cdot1_{\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)}$ is a morphism of presheaves of abelian groups from the constant presheaf $U\mapsto\mathbf Z/p\mathbf Z$ to the sheaf $\mathbf G_a$ [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-descent], so it factors uniquely through the sheafification $\eta:\underline{\mathbf Z/p}\to\mathbf F_p$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], [def-sc-constant-sheaves]: this is $\iota$, with $\iota_U\circ\eta_U(c)=c\cdot1$. Finally $\wp\circ\iota\circ\eta=0$ because $c^p=c$ in $\mathbf Z/p\mathbf Z$ (Fermat), so $\wp\circ\iota=0$ by the uniqueness in the universal property (the zero morphism also factors $0$).

proof.text: *$\wp$ is an epimorphism* (following the proof of the Kummer sequence, Stacks Lemma 03PL). By [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] it suffices to show: for every object $U$ of $C_{\Et}$ and $f\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ there is a covering $\{V_i\to U\}$ in $C_{\Et}$ with $f|_{V_i}=y_i^p-y_i$ for some $y_i\in\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal O_{V_i})$. Cover $U$ by affine opens $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ [def-pc-scheme], let $f_i=f|_{U_i}\in A_i$ and $B_i=A_i[T]/(Q_i)$ with $Q_i=T^p-T-f_i$, monic. Its derivative is $Q_i'=pT^{p-1}-1=-1$, a unit, so $A_i[T]_{Q_i'}/(Q_i)=B_i$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-monic-derivative](1). It is of finite type, and every geometric fibre, over $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ with $\Omega$ an algebraically closed field, is $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega[T]/(T^p-T-\bar f_i)$, nonempty because a polynomial of degree $p\geq1$ over a field gives a nonzero quotient ring; so $\operatorname{Spec}B_i\to U_i$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-nonempty-fibres]. Put $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$; the composite $V_i\to U_i\hookrightarrow U\to C$ is etale, since open immersions are etale [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] and composites of etale morphisms are etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](2), and $V_i\to U$ is a morphism of $C_{\Et}$. The $U_i$ cover $U$ and each $V_i\to U_i$ is surjective, so $\{V_i\to U\}$ is jointly surjective, a covering of $C_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For $y_i$ the class of $T$ in $B_i$ we have $y_i^p-y_i=f_i=f|_{V_i}$.

proof.text: *The kernel on stalks.* Let $K\to\mathbf G_a$ be a kernel of $\wp$ in the abelian category $\Ab(C_{\Et})$; as $\wp\circ\iota=0$ (step 1), $\iota$ factors as $\iota=(K\to\mathbf G_a)\circ\iota'$ with $\iota':\mathbf F_p\to K$. Let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to C$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. The stalk functor at $\bar x$ is exact [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], so $K_{\bar x}=\ker(\wp_{\bar x})\subseteq(\mathbf G_a)_{\bar x}=\varinjlim_{(U,\bar u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)=:R$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods], where $\wp_{\bar x}[U,\bar u,a]=[U,\bar u,a^p-a]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk], $\mathbf Z/p\to(\mathbf F_p)_{\bar x}$, $c\mapsto[C,\bar x,\eta_C(c)]$, is an isomorphism; composed with $\iota'_{\bar x}$ it is $c\mapsto[C,\bar x,c\cdot1]$. (a) *Injective:* $R\neq0$, since $1=0$ in $R$ would give $1=0$ in some $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ with $U$ nonempty (it receives $\bar u$), impossible; for $c\neq0$ the element $c\cdot1$ is a unit of $R$ ($c$ is invertible in $\mathbf Z/p$), hence nonzero. (b) *Surjective onto $\ker\wp_{\bar x}$:* let $[U,\bar u,a]$ with $[U,\bar u,a^p-a]=0$; after passing to a smaller pointed etale neighbourhood, $a^p=a$ in $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. Let $u\in U$ be the image of $\bar u$. The germ $a_u$ in the local ring $\mathcal O_{U,u}$ satisfies $a_u^p=a_u$ and $p=0$ there, so $a_u=c\cdot1$ for some $c\in\mathbf Z/p$ by [lem-sc-local-ring-artin-schreier-kernel]; hence $a|_W=c\cdot1$ on an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq U$ of $u$. $W\to C$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], and $\bar u$ factors through $W$ (its image point $u$ lies in the open $W$), so $(W,\bar u)$ is a pointed etale neighbourhood over $(U,\bar u)$ and $[U,\bar u,a]=[W,\bar u,c\cdot1]=[C,\bar x,c\cdot1]$. Thus $\iota'_{\bar x}$ is bijective for every geometric point.

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By step 3, $\iota':\mathbf F_p\to K$ is an isomorphism on every geometric stalk, hence an isomorphism of $\Ab(C_{\Et})$ [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. So $\iota=(K\to\mathbf G_a)\circ\iota'$ is a kernel of $\wp$; in particular it is a monomorphism and $\operatorname{Im}(\iota)=\operatorname{Ker}(\wp)$. With $\wp\circ\iota=0$ (step 1) and $\wp$ an epimorphism (step 2), the sequence $0\to\mathbf F_p\to\mathbf G_a\to\mathbf G_a\to0$ is short exact by the definition [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence].
